name: Virginia CDPA
law: Virginia Consumer Data Protection Act (Va. Code Title 59.1, Chapter 53, § 59.1-575 et seq.)

deadline.text: Within 45 days of receipt of the request. The controller may extend this once by a further 45 days where reasonably necessary, provided it informs you of the extension and the reason within the first 45 days.

US-VA.name: Office of the Attorney General of Virginia

text.en: Please confirm whether you are processing my personal data and, if so, provide me with access to that personal data. Please also provide the information you are required to give in response to such a request.

Please correct the inaccuracies in my personal data that you hold, as specified in this request, taking into account the nature of the data and the purposes of the processing. Please confirm in writing once the correction has been made.

Please delete the personal data that I provided to you or that you have obtained about me, and confirm in writing once this has been done. Where you rely on a statutory exception to retain any of it, please tell me which one.

Please provide me with a copy of the personal data that I previously provided to you, in a portable and, to the extent technically feasible, readily usable format that allows me to transmit it to another controller without hindrance.

I opt out of the processing of my personal data for the purposes of targeted advertising, the sale of my personal data, and profiling in furtherance of decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects concerning me. Please confirm in writing that you have honored this request.

sources.title: Va. Code § 59.1-577 Personal data rights; consumers (Virginia Law Information System)
Virginia Attorney General: Consumer Data Protection Act summary

notes: Applies only to Virginia residents acting in an individual or household context, and only to businesses that meet the Act's thresholds. The portability right covers only data you previously provided to the controller. The Act has no consent-withdrawal right as such. The numbering of subdivisions A(1) to A(5) follows the order of rights in the official text; the opt-out subdivision text was truncated in the retrieved copy. The Act gives no private right of action; the Attorney General enforces it.
